Use case: sketch-to-render. Create one polished photorealistic square FRONT architectural image for a house concept PDF.
Image 1 is the PRIMARY reference: a perspective model built from the actual measurements. Preserve its broad 9 m facade, two-story massing, all window and door positions, and 5.5 m front court. Image 2 supplies ONLY warm materials, the flower-shaped terracotta screen pattern, courtyard gate, tropical planting and late-afternoon atmosphere. Image 3 gives exact front opening widths. Override Image 2's narrower/taller massing with Image 1's dimensions.
Render the measured model as a real warm Mexican contemporary home in Las Juntas, Puerto Vallarta. 10 m lot frontage, 9 m building width, 1 m left side passage, one car on the left, right pedestrian gate and path to the near-center timber entrance. Ground clear ceiling 3.0 m, upper floor 3.4 m, upper clear ceiling 2.8 m. Upper ceiling 6.2 m; simple low roof cap around 6.7 m for visualization. Give the facade a broad balanced width-to-height relationship like the model. Keep the roof line approximately level across the facade; do not create an extra-tall stair tower.
There are TWO small, high frosted bathroom windows on the upper left: widths 0.70 m and 0.90 m, separated by solid wall. Downstairs there is one 0.85 m bathroom window at left and one narrow 0.45 m laundry window near the entrance. The 1.0 m entrance door starts 4.10 m from the BUILDING left edge. No large front bedroom window.
Replace the model's orange grid with a beautifully detailed OPEN terracotta flower-pattern celosia, like Image 2, about 2.15 m wide on the right and visually spanning both stories. Two separate 1.65 m stair-window groups remain behind it, one per floor, with solid wall/floor between. The glass is behind the clay blocks. Keep the screen mostly visible with restrained planting.
Warm cream plaster, dark bronze frames and slatted gate, timber entry, compact-car scale, subtle terracotta/patterned details. No extra windows, doors, balconies, roof deck or pool. Add realistic tropical urban setting without changing the house geometry. Camera should follow the measured model's broad frontal view, straight verticals and realistic proportions; frame to include courtyard and sky. Do not reproduce model lines, labels, borders or the cuboid car: use one real compact car. No text, numbers, watermarks or logos.

Use case: sketch-to-render.
Create a photorealistic warm Mexican contemporary rear garden view of this EXACT measured house model. The single attached drawing is the controlling geometry, not just inspiration. Preserve the drawn two-story silhouette and opening arrangement. Match the same camera direction, but use a slightly oblique view from the garden-right so that the depth step between floors is clearly visible at the right side.
CRITICAL GEOMETRY: The ground-floor rear wall is 9 m wide. The upper rear wall is also 9 m wide and is recessed 1 m BEHIND the lower wall, creating a continuous narrow flat roof shelf above the lower floor. This shelf must be clearly visible as a projecting cream horizontal ledge above the canopy, including a bare exposed portion at viewer right. The upper wall continues up from BEHIND that shelf. Upper floor starts at 3.4 m; total two-story height approximately 6.7 m. The topmost roof line is ONE flat simple cap. No third-story box or extra raised mass behind the roof. This is a 10 m-wide lot with a 1 m side passage on viewer RIGHT.
There is only one upper window: 3.05 m wide, on the LEFT. The RIGHT upper half is solid cream wall. Ground floor has a 3.2 m sliding glass door LEFT and a 2.9 m living window RIGHT with a solid sill. Keep a pier between the two. No other rear windows or doors.
The lower terrace canopy is 6 m wide and 3 m deep, offset toward viewer-left, not the full building width. Match the model's two posts and canopy attachment. Keep a visibly uncovered section of the ground-floor wall and ground at viewer RIGHT. There is only 1 m of narrow garden beyond the 3 m terrace. Do not lengthen the yard or create a large lawn.
MATERIALS AND CHARACTER: warm cream textured stucco, slim dark bronze window frames, slender dark metal canopy posts and fascia, warm timber canopy soffit, clay-red and cream geometric terracotta terrace tiles, timber outdoor dining table and eight woven chairs, modest tropical plants, warm subtle lamps. Inside the rear-left door is the dining area with kitchen beyond; inside the rear-right window is the lounge. Atmospheric late afternoon in Las Juntas near Puerto Vallarta, realistic architectural photography, straight verticals.
Convert the model's simple blocks into real materials without redesigning its building shape. No diagram lines, writing, dimension numbers, logos or watermarks. No balcony, rooftop furniture, people or pool. Square final image.
